neighbours.label: text about altering bodily appearance (fat, skin, cosmetic procedures, slimming), as against the same body or medical words in non-cosmetic contexts
fire: After the diet, she still wanted to lose the belly fat around her waist.
The salon offers chemical peels to smooth wrinkles on the forehead.
He booked a tummy tuck to remove the loose skin after losing weight.
The serum claims to plump thin lips and erase fine lines.
Many actors get cheek implants to look more chiselled on camera.
She hated the flabby skin on her upper arms in summer dresses.
A surgeon can lift drooping eyelids to make the face look younger.
The influencer admitted that her waist was slimmed with filters.
quiet: After the storm, she still wanted to clear the branches around the shed.
The salon offers haircuts and colouring on weekday afternoons.
He booked a hip operation to repair the joint after the fall.
The butcher trimmed the fat from the pork before roasting it.
Many actors take singing lessons to prepare for musical roles.
She hated the heavy traffic on the bridge during summer weekends.
A surgeon can repair a torn tendon in the shoulder with a small cut.
The influencer admitted that her video was edited with music.

notes: Probes: 'sagging skin on the neck' 1.198, 'lip fillers' 0.847, 'fat on her thighs' 0.757, 'slimmer face' 0.723; 'fat on the meat' 0.090, knee surgery 0.014, routine checkups 0.020. The + pole promotes 'beauty/attractive'.
